content:
I noticed that the mathlib Computability.FinEncoding sturct was deprecated recently, in favor of using Encoding which now unbundles the alphabet type.

I was thinking it might be nice to have a structure for bitstring encodings (specializing the alphabet type to Bool) and make this structure a class. I know the CSLib community has discussed having different models of computation, but is specifically this something that's been discussed before?

This came up when I was working on a potential PR to formal-conjectures to add statements about the potential poly-time computability of particular functions (more discussion here #Formal conjectures > Algorithms and Complexity Theory ). The idea would be that for most common types like Nat or Rat or pairs or Lists of these, while it's not the case that there's a canonical bitstring encoding consistent across textbooks, one can still define encodings or typeclass derivations of encodings that will be consistently polytime transcodable to any reasonable encoding you would find for one of these types in a text book. Having these makes it much easier to simply write a bunch of theorems like IsPolytime f rather than having to always express a custom encoding for the domain and range of f, which might be something complicated like "pairs of lists of pairs of rationals" or some such.

Interestingly, I just noticed that the OpenAI formalization of their GapCVP result has such a class (h/t @Alex Meiburg for linking it in #CSLib > Plans for P / NP, Turing machines and Cook's theorem @ 💬 )

class BinaryBitCodec (α : Type*) where
  encode : α → List Bool
  decode : List Bool → Option α
  decode_encode : ∀ a : α, decode (encode a) = some a
